clue.text: 23's work broadcast by name, for love trebly complicated

indicators.note: something complicated is tangled up, so the letters of these words are jumbled into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
love is nil in tennis, the letter O, and trebly asks for three of them
broadcast is the past tense of sow when seed is scattered by hand, so it gives SOWN

explanation.surface: A writer's book read out on the radio, its title muddled by a love triangle gone thrice as messy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complicated' rearranges NAME, FOR and three Os into AROOMOFONE; 'broadcast' is not an anagram signal here but the scattering of seed, SOWN. 23 is WOOLF, so 23's work is a Virginia Woolf title.
explanation.definitionFit: Virginia Woolf's 1929 essay on women and writing bears this title, so it is one of her works.

clue.text: Old king is a real help on the water, say?

indicators.note: say signals that the words are to be spoken, so the entry matches the sound of the phrase

parts.words: a real help on the water
parts.note: a tiller is the handle that steers a boat, a real help when sailing; in a non-rhotic British accent 'a tiller' is said like the king's name

explanation.surface: Asks whether an ancient monarch was a great asset to sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech the final R of 'a tiller' is silent, which makes the match.
explanation.definitionFit: Attila ruled the Huns in the fifth century, so he is a king from long ago.

clue.text: Second of colours on the spectrum

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: in red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet the colour comes second.
explanation.definitionFit: In the usual listing of rainbow hues this one follows red, making it the second colour of the visible band.

taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: In Roman Catholic worship a monstrance is the ornate holder in which the consecrated host is displayed.

explanation.walkthrough: The 9" is a sly instruction: nine inches is three-quarters of a foot, so take three-quarters of FOOT. LIP 'cut' loses its P.
explanation.definitionFit: A folio is a single leaf of a book or manuscript, one sheet of paper.

clue.text: 23's work for setter

explanation.surface: A writer's book offered in place of the crossword compiler.
explanation.definitionFit: Woolf's 1928 novel about a gender-changing nobleman shares its title with the pseudonym of a long-serving Guardian compiler.

clue.text: Youngster not quite standing with sitting fetish

explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims BOY to BO; 'standing' turns it upright in this down entry to give OB.
explanation.definitionFit: A fetish is a fixation, something a person is unhealthily preoccupied with.

clue.text: Retreat with ability, but no leadership

explanation.definitionFit: A den or hideaway is a place an animal or person retreats to, so as a noun it fits.

clue.text: In the end, surgeon has treated serious 5 down

explanation.walkthrough: 'treated' rearranges SERIOUS into EUROSIS. 5 down is OBSESSION.
explanation.definitionFit: An obsession is a classic kind of mental disorder of anxiety, a compulsive preoccupation.

clue.text: Further work apparent, I'm heading for exit

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter

explanation.walkthrough: 'heading for' takes E, the first letter of exit; 'heading for exit' reads as leaving.
explanation.definitionFit: Time worked beyond the usual hours is extra labour on top of normal duties.

clue.text: See 12
Languor shown by celebrity dog around the house, or not

parts.note: Lassie is the famous collie of films and television

parts.note: the Tudors were a royal house of England

explanation.surface: A famous dog lazing about the home, or perhaps not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the house' is not a home but a royal dynasty, the Tudors; 'or not' removes those two letters. Lassie is the collie of film and television fame.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe a weary, listless lack of energy, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: See 26
Rolling stock with old tat possibly kept in mind

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: A train that runs to meet ships at a port is a type of railway vehicle, which is what rolling stock means.

clue.text: Y chromosome the culprit?

explanation.definitionFit: A malefactor is a person who does wrong, an offender or criminal.

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

clue.text: Lookin' to preserve fuel, petrol finally having gone up a huge amount

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter

explanation.walkthrough: The dropped G of Lookin' tells you to drop the G of the synonym too. In this down entry 'having gone up' makes the fuel plus petrol's last letter read upwards, giving LLIO.

clue.text: Second name — delicate about it

parts.note: subtle means fine or delicate

clue.text: Forger not wanting to be seen around university

explanation.definitionFit: A smithy is a blacksmith's workshop, and by extension the smith himself, someone who shapes iron at a forge.

clue.text: Familiar nutcracker finally cracking nut

explanation.walkthrough: 'a minimum of' tact is just T, 'involving' in CUE.
